question_text: The following data are obtained for a nickel-iron alloy during the generation of a steady-state ferromagnetic hysteresis loop: \begin{tabular}{cc} \hline $\boldsymbol{H}$ (amperes/m) & $\boldsymbol{B}\left(\right.$ weber $\left./ \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{2}}\right)$ \\ \hline 50 & 0.95 \\ 25 & 0.94 \\ 0 & 0.92 \\ -10 & 0.90 \\ -15 & 0.75 \\ -20 & -0.55 \\ -25 & -0.87 \\ -50 & -0.95 \\ \hline \end{tabular} (a) Plot the data. (b) What is the remanent induction? (c) What is the coercive field? Give your answer as a tuple: (remanent_induction, coercive_field).The units of each required answer are (Wb/m^2, A/m), respectively.
response:
## Analysis

**(a) Plot** — The data traces the descending branch of a ferromagnetic hysteresis loop for the Ni-Fe alloy: $B$ stays high (~0.9) as $H$ drops from 50 to −10, then drops sharply between $H=-15$ and $H=-20$, and saturates near −0.95 for $H=-50$.

**(b) Remanent induction** — This is $B$ at $H=0$:

$$B_r = 0.92\ \text{Wb/m}^2$$

**(c) Coercive field** — This is $H$ at $B=0$. From the table, $B$ crosses zero between $(H=-15,\ B=0.75)$ and $(H=-20,\ B=-0.55)$. Linear interpolation:

$$H_c = -15 + \frac{0-0.75}{-0.55-0.75}(-20+15) = -15 - 2.885 \approx -17.88\ \text{A/m}$$

$$\boxed{(0.92,\ -17.88)}$$
